decision.title: XSLT conformance sweep: instruction locations, next-match in attribute sets, parameter and static error codes (packet 4.28)
decision.summary: Expressions an XSLT instruction adds take the span of its start tag so its errors have a line, xsl:next-match and xsl:apply-imports work in attribute sets, and defaults raise XTTE0600.

body.p: , after , , , . Verified as asks: the debug preset (the xslt, xslt_declaration, xslt_key, xslt_read, xslt_lower_control and cli tests), clang-tidy on the changed files, the call-cycle check, the book examples (, 397 match), and the whole XT40 suite with the release driver after each change, case by case. *XT40 12,239 to 12,250 passed (107 to 104 wrong error), 279 to 268 failed, 0 errors, no case lost**, from a whole run at c238bc6 (with 2.25's commits up to it). Commits 8ea4281, 47981ac, d02aba3, ff27d21.

item.p: Locations of instruction errors ('s open item): the sequence constructor gives the expressions a child's lowering added without a span the span of the child's start tag (src/xslt_lower.c, locate_child_expressions); XPath text keeps its spans. A dynamic or type error an instruction raises (validation XTTE errors, XTDE1490, xsl:message terminate, streamed reads) now has its module and line: $err:module and $err:line-number in xsl:catch (try-004, try-021) and "file.xsl:LINE:COLUMN" in the CLI; the book's two XTTE examples (xsd-typed-data.md) and two CLI tests changed with it.

xsl:next-match and xsl:apply-imports in attribute sets (6.11, 10.2: invoking an attribute set leaves the current template rule): lowered directly in a set's body with a focus, they apply templates to the set's focus slots with empty parameter maps, and the evaluator reads its current rule (next-match-012, attribute-set-0108). A template with context-item use="absent" has none: XTDE0560 (next-match-029). Deviation: a set invoked inside xsl:for-each (or another changed focus) of a template rule still sees that rule, which 6.11 clears; the lowering clears it lexically and the set is a function of its own. Fixing it would take a third variant of each attribute set function or an evaluator operation that clears the rule.

Parameter codes (9.3, 7.2): an explicit default (select or content) that cannot be coerced is XTTE0600 for template and function parameters (sxml_xslt_default_value_mapping; error-0600a, function-40-903); the implicit () keeps XPTY0004 (function-40-904); an implicitly mandatory xsl:iterate parameter is XTSE3520 (error-3520a, iterate-902).

Static checks: XTSE3088 (context-item as with use="absent"), XTSE1210 (unknown key collation), XTSE0500 (visibility without name), XTSE0085 (extension-element-prefixes on a reserved namespace; the suite's XTSE0800 for extension-functions-0105 is not in the draft), XTSE0010 for an xsl:fallback after the text of xsl:select (10.4.2).

Found for the XPath sweep (src/xpath_lower.c, compatible_argument_row): XPath 1.0 compatibility mode converts arguments by fn:number only for xs:double parameters (XPath 4.0, 3.4.1), but F&O 4.0 types the XPath 1.0 number parameters as xs:numeric (fn:round, fn:floor, fn:substring, fn:format-number), so format-number('foo', ...) in a 1.0 stylesheet is XPTY0004. Treating xs:numeric and xs:numeric? like xs:double, measured in a private build only, passes 8 cases (format-number-014, -035, -038 to -041, backwards-022, xpath-compat-0401) and is the reading the suite takes.

The draft decides, left (): numerics compare exactly in 4.0 (sx-gc-eq-016, -020, -021, -116, -120, -121); union patterns take the lowest priority and predicates +0.5 (next-match-025a, -026a, priority-002, -124, -141, -163, conflict-resolution-1901a); XPDY0002 for unparsed-entity functions without a focus (error-1370a, -1380a, context-item-016); XTDE0050, not XTDE0700, for a global parameter (error-0610d).

Left, with causes: suite inconsistencies (package-location-001 to -005 read a missing file and assert @q where @p is written; next-match-017 leaves out an xsl:text newline; whitespace-only assert-xml in sf-snapshot-0201 to -0209, attribute-set-1508/-1509); date-094e/f and 095e/f assume no processor supports years past 2^32 (sxml does); FORG0001 where a cast in a binding's coercion fails (as-1602, sequence-0132, variable-0115, call-template-ext-2102: a mapping would also catch FORG0001 of lazily evaluated values); XTTE0945 for xsl:copy with a dynamically absent focus (copy-4308, glob-cxt-item-013); 's per-package strip-space for fn:document, fragment identifiers of xsl:source-document (implementation-defined), strip-space "none" of an available document, namespace-2606.
The XT40 section of docs/CONFORMANCE.md was not regenerated.
